title: seed: the shared seed-datasets replay list is append-only, so after a package upgrade it keeps the superseded version's datasets until restart — new orgs replay old and new seed sets
body:
triage#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH

Filed by triage at the request of repo:objectstack#1 (area o1-D, mailbox #32588, 6968409010), from the contract review of PR #35065 (6968234700, M2) and seat ruling 6968296038.

## What happens
The shared `seed-datasets` list that per-org seed replay reads is **append-only**. After a package upgrade, the old version's datasets stay on the list until the process restarts. An organization created between the upgrade and the restart therefore replays the **superseded** seed sets beside the new ones. For example, two fallback-marked declarations of one object can coexist, which is the case PR #35065 now refuses at the fallback choice.

## Done when
- An upgrade replaces (not appends) the upgraded package's entries on the shared list, keyed by package and dataset, so the list matches the installed version without a restart.
- A pin covers install v1, upgrade to v2, then create an org: only v2's seed sets are replayed.

Related: #34940 / PR #35065 (`Seed.fallback`), #35086 (replay errors at info).
Grade: **p2 · domain:server**. Theme: install, upgrade and uninstall reliability, with an effect on new orgs after an upgrade until restart. No customer is named, so p2. It goes to the p2 queue; no p2 seat is online right now.
